nodes.description: Reduced electron flux through the respiratory chain lowers oxidative phosphorylation and forces a shift to anaerobic glycolysis, elevating lactate and producing lactic acidosis. Energy-demanding post-mitotic tissues (brain, skeletal muscle, optic nerve, and sometimes heart) are preferentially affected, giving the characteristic Leigh-spectrum and multisystem phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic dichotomy in mitochondrial complex II genetic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Genetic disorders of the mitochondrial respiratory chain are often characterized by hypotonia, growth retardation, cardiomyopathy, myopathy, neuropathy, organ failure, and metabolic derangement.

nodes.description: Dilated cardiomyopathy from cardiomyocyte energy failure; can present in the neonatal period.

evidence.reference_title: Familial neonatal isolated cardiomyopathy caused by a mutation in the flavoprotein subunit of succinate dehydrogenase.
evidence.snippet: we present the association of a mutation in the SDHA gene with recessive neonatal isolated DCM in 15 patients of two large consanguineous Bedouin families.

nodes.description: Subacute necrotizing encephalopathy (Leigh syndrome), the most common presentation of SDHA complex II deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of a nuclear succinate dehydrogenase gene results in mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency.
evidence.snippet: We now report a mutation in the nuclear-encoded flavoprotein (Fp) subunit gene of the succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) in two siblings with complex II deficiency presenting as Leigh syndrome.

nodes.description: Deficient complex II activity impairs FAD-dependent oxidation of succinate to fumarate and the transfer of electrons through the SDHB iron-sulfur clusters to ubiquinone, disrupting the junction between the TCA cycle and the respiratory electron transport chain.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic dichotomy in mitochondrial complex II genetic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Complex II oxidizes succinate to fumarate in the Krebs cycle and is involved in the mitochondrial electron transport chain.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of a nuclear succinate dehydrogenase gene results in mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The deleterious effect of the Arg to Trp substitution on the catalytic activity of SDH was observed in a SDH- yeast strain transformed with mutant Fp cDNA.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SDHA reduce or destabilize the catalytic flavoprotein subunit of succinate dehydrogenase, lowering steady-state levels of assembled complex II and the amount of catalytically active enzyme in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

evidence.reference_title: SDHA mutations causing a multisystem mitochondrial disease: novel mutations and genetic overlap with hereditary tumors.
evidence.snippet: Here, we characterize four patients with isolated complex II deficiency caused by mutations in SDHA presenting with multisystem mitochondrial disease including Leigh syndrome (LS) and/or leukodystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Recessive germline SDHA and SDHB mutations causing leukodystrophy and isolated mitochondrial complex II deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Western blotting and BN-PAGE studies confirmed decreased steady-state levels of the relevant SDH subunits and impairment of complex II assembly.

nodes.description: Missense variant near the FAD-binding region that severely reduces complex II activity; pathogenicity confirmed by lentiviral complementation of patient fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: SDHA mutations causing a multisystem mitochondrial disease: novel mutations and genetic overlap with hereditary tumors.
evidence.snippet: For the third new mutation, c.565T>G, we show that it severely affects enzyme activity. Its pathogenicity was confirmed by lentiviral complementation experiments on the fibroblasts of patients carrying this mutation.

nodes.description: Homozygous Arg554Trp substitution in the flavoprotein subunit reported by Bourgeron et al. in two siblings with complex II deficiency presenting as Leigh syndrome - the first nuclear gene mutation shown to cause a human mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency.
